notice.title: What is saved, and where
notice.body: Everything below is saved on the computer that runs CA Mode: this computer, or the server your team hosts it on. Your profile name, a scrypt hash of your PIN, the optional profile details, savings goals and decisions you enter yourself, your INDmoney connection tokens and, with Google sign-in, your Google account ID and email address. CA Mode never saves details the assistant infers from your chats. If you choose to save history: your chats (each kept 30 days after its last message, at most 50) and a daily snapshot of your INDmoney net worth, allocation and holdings for the retention period you pick, the holdings from any CAS statement you upload (the last 12; never the PDF, its password, or your name, PAN or contact details), and the portfolio change investigations you run (the last 50: the snapshots compared, the figures computed from them, the checks and the result), and a record of the steps behind each chat answer (the last 200, none older than 30 days: the start of your question, which data was read and a short preview of it, the figures CA Mode calculated from it, the checks on the answer and how long each step took; never the answer itself or your PIN, tokens or PAN). Everything is in a SQLite file readable only by the account that runs CA Mode. INDmoney tokens are encrypted with a key kept outside that file.

notice.title: Locked with your PIN
notice.body: Your saved chats, answer records, portfolio snapshots, investigations, CAS holdings, profile details, goals and decisions are encrypted with a key that only your PIN or your recovery code can unlock. Other profiles, and anyone with a copy of the database, cannot read them. Whoever runs a hosted copy could change the app to capture your PIN, so only use one run by someone you trust. After the app restarts you enter your PIN again. If you forget your PIN, your recovery code lets you set a new one. If you lose both, your saved history cannot be recovered by anyone.

notice.title: Signing in with Google
notice.body: Where CA Mode is set up for Google sign-in, Google tells CA Mode your Google account ID, email address, whether it is verified, and your name. CA Mode keeps the account ID and email address (the address encrypted with the same key as INDmoney tokens) to know which profile is yours, and uses your name only to suggest a profile name; it never sees your Google password and has no access to your Gmail, Drive, contacts or anything else in your Google account. Google learns that you signed in to CA Mode, under Google's own privacy policy. Signing in does not unlock your saved history: your PIN still does. The account link is part of your export and is deleted with your profile.

notice.title: What whoever runs CA Mode can see
notice.body: Where an admin page is turned on, the people who run this copy can see a list of profiles with each one's name, Google email address, plan, the number of questions asked today, when it was created and last used, whether it accepted this notice, whether INDmoney is connected and when the last snapshot was taken, and whether its PIN is locked after wrong guesses. From that page they can change your plan, clear a PIN lock, sign your profile out on every device, or delete your profile and everything it owns. The admin page cannot open your PIN-locked history: your chats, goals, decisions, profile details and portfolio snapshots are not shown there.

notice.title: Where your questions go
notice.body: To answer you, your message, recent chat history, and the profile details, goals and decisions that bear on your question (with figures calculated from them) go to the AI model you select, along with any INDmoney or snapshot data Portfolio Analyzer reads for that answer. With Ollama the model runs on a computer controlled by whoever runs CA Mode (this computer, or for a hosted copy the operator's own machine, reached over an encrypted private network) and is not sent to any AI company. With OpenAI or Groq it is sent to that company and handled under its own data policy. Portfolio Analyzer reads from INDmoney with read-only access and cannot trade or move money.

notice.title: Private mode
notice.body: Chats are kept in memory only and are gone when you sign out or the app restarts. No portfolio snapshots are taken, CAS statements cannot be uploaded, investigations and answer records are not saved, and switching to private mode deletes the chats, answer records, snapshots, investigations and CAS holdings already saved for this profile. Your INDmoney connection tokens, profile details, goals and decisions are still saved; disconnect INDmoney or remove your saved goals and decisions on the Goals page to delete them.

notice.title: In your browser
notice.body: CA Mode sets one cookie, which keeps this browser signed in to your profile (and, during Google sign-in, ties Google's answer to this browser), and remembers your theme, agent and model choice in this browser. It has no advertising and no third-party analytics or tracking. Pages load fonts from Google Fonts and the chart library from cdn.plot.ly, so those services see this computer's IP address when the app opens.

notice.title: Page-view counts
notice.body: If you save history, CA Mode adds one to a daily count each time you open one of its pages, such as Goals or Portfolio Overview. Only the date, the page name and the number are stored: not your profile, what you typed, which chat or investigation you opened, your IP address or your browser. The counts stay in the same SQLite file for 90 days, are never sent anywhere, and can be read by whoever runs CA Mode. Because they are not linked to you, they are not part of your export and are not removed when you clear history or delete your profile. Private mode is never counted.

notice.title: Usage limits
notice.body: A copy of CA Mode shared with other people may limit how much it can be used; a copy for one computer has no limits unless whoever runs it sets them. Your profile's plan (Free, Individual or Team) is stored with it, changed only by whoever runs this copy, and is part of your export; the daily question limit applies only to the Free plan. With a daily question limit, the number of questions your profile asked today and yesterday is stored (never what you asked); it is not part of your export and is deleted with your profile. With request rate limits, the times of recent requests from your IP address and profile are kept in memory only, for about an hour at most, and never saved. If sign-up includes a Cloudflare Turnstile check, the sign-up form loads it from challenges.cloudflare.com, which sees your IP address and browser details to tell people from bots.

notice.title: Your controls
notice.body: From your profile you can change these choices at any time, export your data, clear your saved history, disconnect INDmoney, or delete the profile and everything stored for it. The Goals page shows the goals, decisions and profile details the assistant can use, and lets you edit or remove them.

tools.name: lookup_ind_keys
tools.description:
Used to resolve stock, index, derivative, commodity, or mutual fund names into valid identifiers.

        Always use this tool first when the user mentions a stock, index, ticker, derivative, or fund
        by name. Do not guess ind_key values manually.

        Use filter_type="IN_COMMODITY" for MCX commodities — gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas and
        the base metals. These are NOT covered by IN_STOCKS_FNO, which searches equity and index
        derivatives only and will return unrelated equity options for a commodity name (a query for
        "crude oil" matches HINDPETRO options there).

        For a commodity, this returns the FUTURES contract, which is the key every downstream tool
        takes — the option chain, details and candles all work on it. Ask for a strike or a side
        ("goldm 160000 call") to get a specific option leg instead.

        Returns the best matching identifiers for the provided names, along with readable display
        names. Use the returned ind_key values in downstream tools. A name that could not be
        searched comes back as {"ind_key": null, "name", "error"} saying how to retry it; the
        other names in the call are unaffected.

tools.name: networth_snapshot
tools.description:
Fetch the user's overall net worth snapshot across the full portfolio.

        Use for:
          - total net worth, total wealth, or broad portfolio summary
          - total invested amount and current portfolio value
          - allocation across investment types and asset classes
          - market-cap split of directly held Indian and US stocks
          - liabilities such as loans, EMIs, and credit card dues
          - overall portfolio health, diversification, or total P&L

        sector rows are always empty (the portfolio tracking backend has no
        sector analytics), and market_cap covers directly held stocks only —
        mutual fund underlying exposure is not included.

        Pass family_member (a name from get_family_members) to fetch a family
        member's snapshot instead of the user's own.

        Call this immediately when the user refers to "my net worth", "my portfolio", "my
        wealth", or wants an overall view of their holdings. The data lives in INDmoney — never
        ask the user to paste or provide their portfolio; always fetch it here first.

tools.name: networth_allocation_breakdown
tools.description:
Analyze one specific asset type and return its allocation breakdown.

        Use for:
          - analysis of a specific asset type such as MF, IND_STOCK, or US_STOCK
          - asset-class-wise breakdown for that asset type
          - market-cap-wise breakdown of directly held stocks (IND_STOCK / US_STOCK)
          - focused asset analysis instead of the full net worth snapshot

        Sector breakdowns are no longer available (the portfolio tracking
        backend has no sector analytics) and return empty rows with a
        data_note. market_cap buckets only directly held stocks — for MF and
        other indirect assets it returns empty rows with a data_note.

        Pass family_member (a name from get_family_members) to analyze a family
        member's allocation instead of the user's own.

        Call this when the user asks to analyze a specific asset type — e.g. "my MF allocation"
        or "break down my equity/holdings". The data lives in INDmoney — never ask the user to
        paste or provide their holdings; always fetch it here.

tools.name: networth_holdings
tools.description:
Return row-level holdings for one specific asset type.

        Use for:
          - listing holdings within a specific asset type such as IND_STOCK, MF, or BOND
          - units held, unit price, current value, or broker per holding
          - P&L, P&L %, and one-day change for each holding
          - checking whether a specific stock, fund, or bond is present in that asset type
          - comparing invested vs current value per instrument

        The response carries asset_summary (total_value, invested, one-day change
        for the requested asset type) plus per-row holdings. holding_percent is a
        holding's share of the requested asset type's value, not of the whole
        portfolio.

        US_STOCK amounts come in BOTH currencies: INR (invested_amount,
        market_value, one_day_change) and USD (invested_value_usd,
        current_value_usd, one_day_change_usd per row; total_value_usd,
        invested_usd, one_day_change_usd in asset_summary). Quote whichever
        currency the user asks for — both are available — and never add INR and
        USD figures together. For US_STOCK rows investment_code is the ticker
        (e.g. META), usable directly with get_us_stocks_details and
        get_us_stocks_ohlc; for MF rows it is the scheme code.

        INSURANCE and RD are not served by the portfolio tracking backend and
        return empty holdings with a data_note.

        F&O / DERIVATIVES — asset_type="IND_STOCK" is also the source for the user's
        derivative book. There is no separate F&O asset type; use IND_STOCK for
        futures and options positions. Alongside equity holdings it returns:
          - derivative_positions        open + netted F&O legs (futures and options)
          - drv_intra_day_positions     intraday derivative legs
          - positions, intra_day_positions, mtf_positions, strategy_positions
          - commodity_positions, commodity_intra_day_positions
          - open_orders, open_derivative_orders
        Any of these may be null or empty when the user holds nothing in that book.

        Each derivative_positions row carries:
          - position_id       identifier for this leg
          - ind_stock_id      the instrument's ind_key
          - instrument_type   the contract kind, e.g. FUTSTK for a stock future
          - avg_price, buy_avg_price, sell_avg_price, buy_qty, sell_qty
          - quantity          net open quantity; 0 means the leg is fully netted out
          - netting_type      e.g. net_buy / net_sell
          - realised_gains, day_realised_gains

        To analyse a derivative leg, pass its ind_stock_id to get_indian_stocks_details —
        that returns live_price (LTP), expiry_date, open_interest, underlying_parent_ind_key,
        and, for options, greeks_data (delta, theta, vega, gamma, iv_vwap). This tool does
        NOT return LTP or greeks; the two calls together give the full picture of a position.

        For linked (non-INDmoney) brokers, invested_amount is often missing and returned as 0.
        Pass family_member (a name from get_family_members) to fetch a family member's
        holdings instead of the user's own.
        Call this immediately when the user refers to "my stocks", "my holdings", "my positions",
        "my funds", "my F&O positions", "my options", "my futures", or holdings within a specific
        asset type. The data lives in INDmoney — never ask the user to paste or provide their
        holdings or positions; always fetch it here first.

tools.name: get_indian_stocks_ohlc
tools.description:
Use this tool to fetch historical and currently running OHLC candle data
        for an Indian stock, F&O derivative, or index.

        Use for:
          - price history
          - candle charting
          - intraday movement
          - running live candle
          - trend analysis
          - support/resistance
          - breakout/reversal detection
          - volatility expansion
          - momentum confirmation

        Each candle carries datetime_ist (IST wall clock), open, high, low,
        close and volume. At most 250 candles are returned per call — enough
        for a full year of daily candles. When the window holds more (1minute
        over a whole session, for example) the MOST RECENT candles are kept:
        candles_total then carries the full count and data_note says so. For
        the whole window at that point choose a coarser interval (5minute for
        a session, 1day for weeks) rather than paging.

        Every call retrieves an upstream snapshot. retrieved_at_ist is when
        this server received it, not the feed's update time; upstream does not
        provide a source update timestamp for each candle. Call again to refresh.
        On a 1minute call, last_candle_is_current_minute says only whether the
        final candle starts in the minute containing query_end_ist. That candle
        may be partial; its presence does not prove that its OHLCV fields are
        current or updated together. Short windows may be empty when they do
        not overlap a trading session.

tools.name: get_indian_stocks_details
tools.description:
Use this tool to fetch detailed live market information
        for Indian stocks, indices, ETFs, futures, and options.

        Use this tool when the user asks for:
          - current stock details
          - live price / LTP
          - market stats
          - analyst sentiment / ratings
          - target price
          - derivative greeks
          - option/future details
          - bid/ask depth
          - underlying contract info
          - multi-stock comparison

        By default returns core price/market data only.

        segments=["depth"] adds market_depth per instrument: {"NSE": {"bids":
        [{"price", "qty"}...], "asks": [...], "total_bid_qty", "total_ask_qty",
        "bid_pct", "ask_pct"}} — up to 5 levels per exchange, NSE and BSE for a
        stock, one book for a contract. This is the latest available upstream
        snapshot, which can retain an earlier session's book. depth_retrieved_at_ist
        records retrieval time, not feed freshness. Upstream supplies no book
        timestamp: depth_source_updated_at_ist is null and depth_freshness is
        "unknown" when a book is returned. price_updated_at_ist is the quote's
        timestamp and does not date the book. depth_status distinguishes available,
        empty, timeout, unavailable and unsupported; depth_note explains missing
        depth without guessing market status or demat eligibility. The current
        source does not support BSE-only cash instruments. segment_meta_data
        (lot size, tick size, freeze qty)
        rides along for contracts so quantities can be read in lots.

tools.name: get_indian_stocks_option_chain
tools.description:
Use this tool to fetch the live option chain
        for an Indian stock or index underlying.

        Always use this tool when the user asks for:
          - option chain
          - strike-wise OI
          - PCR
          - expiry analysis
          - max pain
          - call vs put buildup
          - support and resistance from OI
          - IV analysis
          - derivatives sentiment
          - ATM / OTM strike comparison
          - per-strike greeks: delta, theta, vega, gamma (both call and put)
          - bid / ask per strike, for spread and liquidity checks
          - per-strike OI reads: oi_shade_tag (SUPPORT / RESISTANCE) and
            oi_trend_tag (short-build-Up / long-unwinding)

        Works for NSE stock/index underlyings and for MCX commodities (gold,
        silver, crude oil, natural gas, base metals) — resolve the commodity
        with lookup_ind_keys(filter_type="IN_COMMODITY") and pass the futures
        key it returns.

        On NSE underlyings each strike carries greeks for both sides, so a
        multi-leg structure (spread, straddle, condor) can be assessed from ONE
        call — do not loop get_indian_stocks_greeks_history per leg for current
        values. MCX chains have NO greeks upstream: the keys are omitted and a
        `greeks_note` says so. Do not substitute greeks_history for them, and do
        not infer greeks from a commodity chain — report OI, volume, price and
        bid/ask, which are complete.

        Upstream field naming varies between responses: bid/ask arrive as either
        ``bp``/``sp`` or ``buy_price``/``sell_price``, and volume as ``v`` or
        ``volume``. Read whichever pair is present rather than assuming one, and
        treat an absent pair as "not quoted" rather than zero.

        Every call retrieves a snapshot; retrieved_at_ist is the retrieval time,
        not a guarantee of feed freshness. Call again to refresh.
        entity_details.price_updated_at_ist is the underlying's own price time
        when available (live-overlaid, price_mode "live"); per-strike rows carry
        no timestamp of their own. identity_fallback: true means upstream was
        re-asked anonymously after an error, so user-specific fields are absent.

        Choose `use_expiry_date=True` when the user specifies expiry.
        Otherwise use nearest expiry automatically.

        `expiry_date` must be an expiry this instrument actually has — take it
        from the `expiry_list` of an earlier call. YYYY-MM-DD and YYYYMMDD are
        both accepted; a date that is not on the list is rejected with the
        valid ones listed, rather than answered with a different expiry.

tools.name: get_indian_stocks_greeks_history
tools.description:
Use this tool whenever the user asks for analysis of an Indian options contract.

        Returns time-series data sampled at 5-minute intervals including:
          - delta, theta, vega (standard option Greeks)
          - iv (implied volatility), iv_vwap (volume-weighted avg IV)
          - charm, volga, veta (higher-order Greeks)
          - tgr (total gamma risk), tv (time value)

        Use for:
          - IV trend analysis over time
          - Greeks evolution across a trading session
          - Theta decay visualization
          - Delta hedging analysis
          - Volatility surface research

        `1d` returns every 5-minute sample. A `7d` window is too long to return
        in full, so it is thinned to evenly spaced samples: `count` is what you
        received, `total_samples` what upstream held, and
        `sampling_interval_minutes` the resulting spacing. Both keys appear only
        when thinning happened. The most recent sample is always the last
        element, so read current values from there rather than assuming the
        series ends at the requested window edge.

        Returns an empty `greeks` list for MCX commodity legs — upstream
        computes no greeks for them at all. Use get_indian_stocks_option_chain
        for commodity OI, price and bid/ask instead.

tools.name: user_watchlist
tools.description:
Fetch the user's own watchlisted instruments from their INDmoney account.

        Pass family_member (a name from get_family_members) to fetch a family
        member's watchlist instead of the user's own.

body.title: Should I keep my emergency fund in a liquid fund or a fixed

messages.content: Should I keep my emergency fund in a liquid fund or a fixed deposit?

For a money‑backing goal that you may need to access on short notice, the **liquid fund** is the more appropriate place to keep your emergency reserve.

**Why liquid funds are usually preferred for an emergency fund**

| Feature | Liquid / Overnight Fund | Fixed Deposit |
|---------|------------------------|---------------|
| **Liquidity** | Withdraw anytime – full amount is usually available in the next business day, no penalty. | Typically locked for a set period (3 months, 6 months, 12 months, etc.). Early withdrawal is possible, but you usually pay a penalty or lose interest. |
| **Risk** | Very low – they invest in government and corporate “money‑market” instruments. | Low, but the risk level depends on the issuing bank’s credit; typically a bank FD is considered very safe as well. |
| **Return** | Usually around the RBI repo rate plus a small spread (≈ 6–7 % per annum, depending on market conditions). | Fixed rate agreed at the time of purchase; often slightly higher than a liquid fund but flat for the lock‑in period. |
| **Suitability for emergency funds** | Matches the CA‑Mode rules: “Liquid and overnight” are explicitly allowed for an emergency fund, “short‑duration debt” is marked “caution” and is still acceptable for an emergency reserve. | Not listed as suitable in the CA‑Mode rules for an emergency fund because of the lack of immediate liquidity. |

Your goal “Emergency fund” has a target of **₹300,000** by 2027‑11‑01, with ₹120,000 already earmarked and a planned monthly contribution of ₹10,000, assuming a 6.5 % annual return. Under those assumptions, the current plan still leaves a shortfall of ₹59,013 unless the monthly contribution is increased to ₹15,193 (or the target reduced, etc.). That calculation shows how critical liquidity is—you need to be able to use the money without waiting for maturities.

**What if you want a slightly higher return?**

You could consider a **short‑term fixed deposit** (e.g., 3–6 months) for part of the amount, especially if you can afford to lock it for that period. The extra return comes at the cost of reduced liquidity and the possibility of a withdrawal penalty. You would still keep the bulk of the emergency fund in a liquid or overnight product.

**Bottom line**

- Keep the **majority** of your emergency reserve in a liquid or overnight fund to satisfy the high‑liquidity requirement and the CA‑Mode suitability rule.  
- If you want to experiment with a short‑term fixed deposit for a portion—be sure you can tolerate that temporary lock‑in and any penalty for early exit.

Remember, the choice isn’t about “bigger returns” but about having the money available when you need it, with minimal risk.

body.title: I want ₹15 lakh for a house down payment in 5 years. How muc

messages.content: I want ₹15 lakh for a house down payment in 5 years. How much should I invest each month if I expect 12% a year?

To reach ₹15 00 000 in 5 years with a 12 % annual return, you would need to invest about **₹18 185 per month** (start of each month, compounding monthly). This figure is a *theoretical illustration* under the constant 12 % assumption; actual returns can vary.

| Scenario | Required monthly contribution |
|----------|------------------------------|
| 0 % return (no growth) | ₹25 000 |
| 10 % annual | ₹19 211 |
| 12 % annual (your assumption) | **₹18 185** |
| 14 % annual | ₹17 202 |

**Risk‑suitability note**  
Under CA Mode’s fixed rules, a goal that needs a fixed amount in a short horizon (5 years) is *allowed* in low‑risk categories such as *Liquid & overnight* and *Short‑duration debt* but is *unsuitable* for equity or higher‑risk hybrid funds. The 12 % assumption is more characteristic of equity markets, so you should verify whether you’re comfortable with the price volatility that comes with that return level.

---

### Next steps – questions that can help fine‑tune your plan

1. **Inflation adjustment** – Do you want the ₹15 00 000 target to grow with inflation (e.g., 3–6 % per year)?
2. **Liquidity need** – Would you need early access to any part of the fund before the 5‑year horizon?
3. **Risk tolerance** – How would a drop in the portfolio’s value affect you during the 5‑year period?

Answering these will let you choose the most appropriate monthly amount and the asset mix that aligns with your risk comfort and timelines.
